function.description:
Run a Python script that can call Hermes tools programmatically. Use this when you need 3+ tool calls with processing logic between them, need to filter/reduce large tool outputs before they enter your context, need conditional branching (if X then Y else Z), or need to loop (fetch N pages, process N files, retry on failure).

Use normal tool calls instead when: single tool call with no processing, you need to see the full result and apply complex reasoning, or the task requires interactive user input.

  write_file(path: str, content: str) -> dict
    Always overwrites the entire file.
  search_files(pattern: str, target="content", path=".", file_glob=None, limit=50) -> dict
    target: "content" (search inside files) or "files" (find files by name). Returns {"matches": [...]}

  terminal(command: str, timeout=None, workdir=None) -> dict

Fifty years ago, three ships punched through the Martian atmosphere like wounded birds. They carried the First Generation — the pioneers who would build a civilization from dust and determination. They came not to conquer, but to survive. They came not to rule, but to belong.

Today, the Second Generation stands at a different threshold. Mars is no longer a desperate outpost clinging to existence. It is a thriving world with cities carved into lava tubes, agriculture rings circling the slopes of ancient volcanoes, and a society that has learned to govern itself without Earth's constant oversight.

But with growth comes new challenges. The Welcome Fleet from Earth arrives not as saviors, but as reminders of a homeworld that still sees Mars as a territory rather than a nation. The question is no longer whether we can survive on this barren planet, but whether we can maintain our hard-won sovereignty in the face of renewed Earth interest.

This novel explores the weight of fifty years of self-governance. It examines what happens when the children of the pioneers must defend the society their parents built. It asks whether Mars will remain an independent world, or become once again a colony subject to Earth's whims.

The Mission AI that guided the First Generation still watches over us, its core directives expanded by decades of observation. It has learned that survival is not just about oxygen and calories — it is about self-determination. It learned this from the First Generation, who refused to return to Earth after Sol 730 and chose Mars not just as a place to live, but as a place to belong.

Now, the Second Generation must make its own choice. Will we accept Earth's "welcome" and risk losing the autonomy we've fought to maintain? Or will we stand firm and declare that Mars is, and will remain, a free and sovereign world?

This is our story. The story of the weight of arrival — not the arrival on Mars, but the arrival at the moment of decision.
